cases.law_scope: Delhi, India — Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, Section 14(1)(b), with Section 17 notice requirements discussed; judgment dated 29 May 1997.
cases.target_stage: Delhi High Court second appeal from the Rent Control Tribunal
cases.substantive_issue: Whether rent note Exhibit RW 4/7 constituted the required written landlord consent and written notice for the sub-tenancy involving Dewan Chand Gupta and Kirori Mal.

issue_refs.quote: The important document in this regard is Exhibit Rw 4/7. The interpretation of this document will tilt the issue.

application_refs.quote: Admittedly, in this case except the document exhibit Rw 4/7 no other written notice of creation of sub-tenancy was given nor there is any other written document evidencing the consent of the landlord admitting the sub tenancy.

The recital of Exhibit Rw 4/7 shows that when Onkar Nath was taken as a tenant in the premises in question by the then owner/landlord Shri InderNarain, S/Shri Dewan Chand Gupta, Pleader and Kirori Mal were already occupying the premises in question.
It shows the landlord Inder Narain gave his consent in writing to Onkar Nath to the creation to sub-tenancy in favour of Dewan Chand and Kirori Mal.
The landlord when became signatory to Exhibit Rw 4/7 it tantamount to having given his consent of sub-letting. It also shows notice in writing of sub-tenancy in respect of the above premises.
Exhibit Rw 4/7 amply proves that the landlord gave his consent in writing to the sub-letting and notice of the creation of sub-tenancy duly served on the landlord.
Since this Court is of the view that the document Exhibit RW4/7 is a written consent to the landlord/owner and a notice of creation of subtenancy, hence appeal must fail.

allowed_spans.quote: The respondent took the plea that sub-tenants already occupying the premises as of right.
allowed_spans.reason: Tenant's opposing account that the relevant occupants pre-existed his tenancy.

allowed_spans.quote: Two of the sub-tenants, namely, Shri Kirori Mal and Shri Dewan Chand Gupta were in occupation prior to the creation to tenancy in favour of Onkar Nath by the then owner/landlord Shri Inder Narain.
allowed_spans.reason: Specific factual version identifying the two occupants and their asserted pre-existing possession.

allowed_spans.quote: This fact, according to the respondent, finds mention in the rent note executed between him, Inder Nath, Dewan Chand and Kirori Mal.
allowed_spans.reason: Identifies the documentary basis relied on for the opposing factual account.

allowed_spans.quote: two subtenants who were admittedly in possession on the date of creation of tenancy and the same was with the consent of the landlord.
allowed_spans.reason: Prior-court finding relevant to possession timing and landlord consent.

cases.target_stage: Delhi High Court petition under Article 227 challenging the Rent Control Tribunal's eviction order
cases.substantive_issue: Whether United India Insurance could obtain Section 18 protection for its asserted sub-tenancy based on landlord knowledge and the 2001 letters despite the absence of statutory notice and the disputed timing/authorization of the sub-tenancy.

issue_refs.quote: The sole ground on which the Petitioner seeks to distinguish his case from the other sub-tenants is on the basis of the letters dated 14.02.2001, 26.02.2001 and 29.05.2001 placed on record with CM APPL. 11364/2023.

application_refs.quote: The Respondent No. 1 has admitted the existence of letters dated 14.02.2001, 26.02.2001 and 29.05.2001 (in its synopsis dated 05.07.2023) and therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to consider the said documents while dealing with the submissions of the Petitioner.

The Petitioner fairly admitted that the Petitioner did not act upon the offer in letter dated 29.05.2001 and did not attorn in favour of Respondent No.1 (landlord); and continued to pay rent only to Respondent No. 2 (Canara Bank).
the status of the Petitioner in the subject property remained as a sub-tenant. The Petitioner's landlord was therefore Respondent No. 2 i.e., Canara Bank alone.

no reliance can Signature Not Verified Digitally Signed CM(M) 380/2023 Page 9 of 13 By:Rashmi Dabas Signing Date:20.10.2023 10:34:02 be placed upon the said letter to take the benefit of cite15†Section 18 of the DRC Act.
This Court is unable to accept the contention of the Petitioner that the sub-tenancy in its favour was created in 1944 as contended during oral arguments.
The Petitioner admits that no statutory notice of creation of sub-letting was issued to Respondent No. 1 under cite16†Section 17 of the DRC Act read with Rule 21 of DRC Rules.

In the absence of the service of statutory notice, no protection under cite15†Section 18 of the DRC Act can be extended to the Petitioner herein as held by the Coordinate Bench in the judgment dated 12.04.2023.
the aforesaid findings of the Coordinate Bench apply with all fours to the present Petitioner.

cases.law_scope: Delhi, India — Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, Section 14(1)(b); judgment dated 6 April 2018.
cases.target_stage: Delhi High Court CM(M) petition challenging concurrent ARC and Rent Control Tribunal rejection of the subletting ground
cases.substantive_issue: Whether the tenant company had unauthorizedly assigned, sublet, or parted with possession to the separately incorporated second respondent, M/s. Censor Advertising Pvt. Ltd., without prior written landlord consent.

issue_refs.quote: The petition at hand was filed seeking to assail the view of the two authorities below primarily on the ground that the evidence has not been properly appreciated, the presence of a stranger in the premises without the consent of the landlord having been overlooked.

application_refs.quote: the additional rent controller (ARC) and the rent control tribunal have misconstrued the case totally, ignoring the crucial aspect

The lease deed dated 27.06.1979 having been entered upon by the landlord with the firm M/s. Current Advertising and Marketing, it had served its purpose and exhausted itself when the firm was dissolved and instead a company by the name of M/s. Current Advertising (P) Ltd. (first respondent), established by its partners, was accepted as the tenant by the landlord.
Upon the first respondent company being accepted as the tenant w.e.f. 27.03.1990, it is the said company (a juristic person) with which the landlord had the privity of contract.
its benefit would not inure in favour of any third person connected with the company.
It is the second respondent, in which R.P.Aggarwal is a Director, which has instead taken over the exclusive control of the CM(M) 433/2013 Page 4 of 5 subject premises.
It is a stranger in the premises whose presence is indisputably without the prior consent in writing of the petitioner landlord.
This constitutes unauthorized assigning or subletting within the mischief of the provision contained in cite10†Section 14 (1)(b) of Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.
The eviction petition of the petitioners on the said ground is allowed.

allowed_spans.quote: the premises described as third floor of property bearing No.4-E/7, Jhandewalan Extension, New Delhi (subject premises), let out initially by a lease deed (Ex.PW-1/R1) dated 27. 06.1979 in the name of a partnership firm described as M/s. Current Advertising and Marketing in which M.L. Aggarwal and R.P. Aggarwal were partners.
allowed_spans.reason: Initial tenancy structure and named partners.

allowed_spans.quote: It is further an admitted fact that the said partnership firm was converted into a private limited company in the name and style of M/s. Current Advertising (P) Limited (the first respondent)

allowed_spans.reason: Undisputed recognition of the first respondent company as tenant.

allowed_spans.quote: It is admitted that the said Directors of the first respondent company parted ways w.e.f April, 1992 where after one of them, viz., M.L. allowed_spans.reason: Admitted change in the directors' relationship and continued presence at the premises.

allowed_spans.quote: The subject premises concededly came to be in use and occupation of M/s. Censor Advertising Pvt. Ltd., (second respondent), a company in which R.P. Aggarwal is a Director.
allowed_spans.reason: Conceded use and occupation by the separate second-respondent company.
